title: AGENTS.md — Open Standard for AI Coding Agents
abstract: AGENTS.md is an emerging open standard for declaring AI agent capabilities, tools, and instructions in a structured markdown file at the root of a repository, enabling consistent agent discovery and interoperability across platforms.
why_we_care: Standardizing how AI agents declare themselves enables our team to build composable, discoverable agent workflows. As we invest in custom agents and MCP servers, having a common metadata format reduces integration friction and makes our agent ecosystem more maintainable. This directly impacts our OLAF skills and agent architecture.
summary: AGENTS.md proposes a standardized way to describe AI agents in repositories — similar to how README.md describes a project for humans, AGENTS.md describes agent capabilities for other agents and orchestrators.
description:
## Overview

AGENTS.md is a proposed open standard (backed by the Linux Foundation) for declaring AI agent metadata in a structured markdown file placed at the root of a repository. It defines agent capabilities, available tools, required permissions, and behavioral instructions in a format that is both human-readable and machine-parseable.

## Key Features

- **Declarative agent metadata**: Name, description, version, capabilities
- **Tool declarations**: What tools the agent can use, with input/output schemas
- **Instruction blocks**: Behavioral guidelines and constraints
- **Interoperability**: Enables agent-to-agent discovery and orchestration
- **Platform-agnostic**: Works across VS Code, GitHub Copilot, and other agent hosts

## Current Status

Early-stage proposal gaining traction in the GitHub/VS Code ecosystem. Several projects have started adopting the pattern informally.
